## First look at your data 👀 {.smaller}

Always start here — **before** any analysis:

```python
df.head()        # first 5 rows
df.shape         # (12, 4) → rows, columns
df.columns       # column names
df.dtypes        # what type is each column?
df.describe()    # quick statistics for numeric columns
```

. . .

> Look at your data first. Most bugs are in the data, not in the code. 🔍

::: notes
8–15 min. Notice: shape and columns have no () — they are attributes, not methods.
Students will mix this up; that's fine, the error message tells them.
:::

## Selecting columns 📏 {.smaller}

One column → a **Series**:

```python
df["gc_content"]
df["gc_content"].mean()     # your average() from Block 1 🎯
df["gc_content"].max()
df["organism"].unique()     # which organisms do we have?
```

. . .

Several columns → a smaller **DataFrame**:

```python
df[["sample", "gc_content"]]      # note: double brackets!
```

::: notes
15–22 min. Double brackets = a list of column names inside the selector.
:::

## Filtering rows 🔎 {.smaller}

Keep only rows where a condition is `True`:

```python
df[df["gc_content"] > 45]
df[df["organism"] == "Homo sapiens"]
```

. . .

Two conditions at once:

```python
df[(df["gc_content"] > 40) & (df["length"] > 1000)]   # AND
df[(df["organism"] == "Mus musculus") | (df["length"] < 900)]   # OR
```

⚠️ In pandas: `&` and `|`, **not** `and` / `or` — and **parentheses** around each condition

::: notes
22–32 min. The & / parentheses rule is the #1 pandas error. Show the error once on purpose.
Connect to week 4: same logic as if, different syntax.
:::

## Sorting & new columns 🔀 {.smaller}

```python
df.sort_values("gc_content")                     # lowest first
df.sort_values("gc_content", ascending=False)    # highest first
df.sort_values("length", ascending=False).head(3)   # top 3 longest
```

. . .

New column from existing ones — **no loop needed** ✨

```python
df["length_kb"] = df["length"] / 1000
df["gc_rich"] = df["gc_content"] > 45
```

::: notes
32–40 min. Point out: pandas applies the operation to every row at once.
In week 5 this would have been a for loop.
:::

## Grouping 🧺 {.smaller}

"What is the mean GC **per organism**?"

```python
df.groupby("organism")["gc_content"].mean()
```

```
organism
Escherichia coli    51.075
Homo sapiens        41.150
Mus musculus        42.775
```

. . .

Read it like a sentence: **group** by organism → take **gc_content** → compute **mean** 🗣️

```python
df.groupby("organism")["length"].max()
df["organism"].value_counts()      # how many samples per organism
```

::: notes
55–63 min. Without pandas: a dictionary of lists + loop (week 6). Mention it, don't code it.
:::

## Saving results 💾

```python
gc_rich = df[df["gc_content"] > 45]
gc_rich.to_csv("results/gc_rich.csv", index=False)
```

. . .

`index=False` → no extra column with row numbers 🧹

Open the file — it's a normal CSV, Excel can read it too 📊

::: notes
63–66 min. Make sure results/ exists, otherwise OSError.
:::

## Cheat sheet 🐼 {.smaller}

| I want to… | pandas |
|---|---|
| read a CSV | `pd.read_csv("file.csv")` |
| look at it | `.head()` · `.shape` · `.describe()` |
| one column | `df["col"]` |
| filter rows | `df[df["col"] > 5]` |
| sort | `df.sort_values("col")` |
| new column | `df["new"] = df["a"] / 1000` |
| per group | `df.groupby("g")["col"].mean()` |
| save | `df.to_csv("out.csv", index=False)` |

## Wrap-up ✅ {.smaller}

- pandas = tables in Python: **DataFrame** 📋 + **Series** 📏
- Look first: `.head()`, `.shape`, `.describe()` 👀
- Filter with `&` / `|` and parentheses ⚠️
- `groupby` = per-group statistics in one line 🧺

**Commit** 💾 your `samples_report.py`.
